cards.key_problem: Physical lab PCs running multiple local VMs are hard to manage, slow to reset and update, and only usable offline in the lab.
key_outcomes: Current state (slide 2): one large desktop per student with multiple VMware Workstation VMs; challenges are physical PC management, reset time, app updates every 2 weeks, offline-only access
Proposed architecture (slide 3): lab VMs and a nested-virtualisation 'master VM' delivered as VDI, with separate lab, user and production networks

Access model (slide 4): a student can use several VMs at once on different virtual switches/VLANs, or a master VM that runs more VMs inside it (Hyper-V/VMware Workstation); campus-wide access with MFA, device lock-in and role/location/device-based zero-trust policies
Benefits (slide 5): no physical PCs, fully automated provisioning and de-provisioning, dynamic sizing, access from anywhere per policy, production network isolated from the lab network
HyLabs summary (slide 6): self-service, timetable-based allocation, non-persistent linked clones, web access for BYOD, role-based security and audit logs

cards.client: Sample log lines taken from a bank's production HySecure deployment
cards.client_actual: The sample logs show a large Indian private bank's UK operation (domain, AD group names and hostnames visible in the raw lines)
cards.key_problem: Customers integrating HySecure with a SIEM or building ARS reports need to know which events HySecure logs, the field order in each log line, and which device attributes identify an endpoint.
key_outcomes: 'Logs Mapping' sheet: 12 events - application request, HyID server auth request, failed application/service access, AD user login, logout and login failure, email authentication request, invalid OTP, native admin login, login failure and logout, failed to send OTP

For each event: a sample log line, a mapping template (<DATESTAMP>,<LOGIN_STATUS_CODE>,<LOGIN_SUBSTATUS_CODE>,... placeholders) and the numbered list of fields reported (status codes, hostname, domain, AD groups, MAC, client and WAN IP, 2FA token type, client type, application server and port, username, application name, EPS profile)

'Device ID' sheet: 17+ attributes HySecure can collect to identify a device (HDD, CPU and motherboard serials, IMEI, MAC list, received and detected WAN IP, device/browser type, browser ID, region, time zone, locale, hostname, domain, default gateway, NIC manufacturer) marked mandatory or optional
The sample lines are unredacted production data: real hostnames, MAC and IP addresses, usernames and the bank's AD group names
